item.title: Spotify shares show mixed performance as CEO Daniel Ek prepares to exit
item.description: Spotify stock is set to close 2025 at around $581 per share, marking a significant increase from the start of the year but a 26% decline from its 52-week high. The mixed performance has prompted questions over the platform’s trajectory heading into 2026, particularly as CEO Daniel Ek prepares to step down. item.title: A tribute to the music industry figures we lost in 2025
item.description: Each year, the African music industry bids farewell to influential voices, executives and creatives whose contributions resonate long after their final works. In 2025, the sector mourned the loss of figures who shaped genres, sparked movements and defined periods in music history, from celebrated performers and studio pioneers to the visionaries behind entire soundscapes. item.title: Nigeria: Shoday shares new single Paparazzi featuring FOLA
item.description: Nigerian Afrobeat artist Shoday has released a new single titled ‘Paparazzi’, featuring FOLA. The track serves as the first official release ahead of his forthcoming project, Hybrid, and is accompanied by a music video directed by Perliks. item.title: MTV music channels shut down as Canal+ strikes Warner Bros. discovery deal
item.description: MTV has closed several music-only video channels across the UK, Europe and South America, ending nearly 40 years of operations outside the United States. The closures, effective 31 December, affect channels including MTV Music, MTV 80s, MTV 90s, Club MTV and MTV Live, with additional services impacted in Australia, Poland, France and Brazil, according to BBC News. item.title: Open call: 2026 METRO FM Music Awards
item.description: The METRO FM Music Awards (MMAs) in South Africa have opened entries for their 2026 edition, inviting eligible South African artists and record companies to submit music released during the current eligibility period. The awards recognise achievements in the South African recording industry over the past year and form part of METRO FM’s annual music honours. Entries are underway and close on 3 February 2026. item.title: Tanzania: Alikiba appoints Kenyan executive Benjamin Otwal as new manager
item.description: Tanzanian musician Ali Kiba has appointed Kenyan music executive Benjamin Otwal as his new manager, a move that signals a shift in his management strategy as he seeks to expand his reach within East Africa and in international markets. The appointment follows a period of professional collaboration between the two, particularly during Ali Kiba’s recent engagements in Kenya. item.title: Kilele Summit 2026 set for Nairobi with international, regional music line-up
item.description: The third edition of the Kilele Summit is scheduled to take place in Nairobi from 23 to 28 February 2026, bringing together musicians, technologists, and culture workers from across East Africa and beyond. Known for its blend of music, art, and culture, the summit features a combination of performances, workshops, installations, and panel discussions. item.title: Napster shuts down music streaming service to focus on AI assistants
item.description: Napster, the once-pioneering music streaming platform, has abruptly ended its music streaming operations following its acquisition by AI company Infinite Reality, signalling a significant shift in the company’s business model towards artificial intelligence. item.title: Spotify to end access to ‘Basic’ music-only plan for subscribers who cancel
item.description: Spotify has introduced a significant restriction to its music-only ‘Basic’ subscription, confirming that subscribers who cancel the plan will permanently lose access to it, raising questions about whether the company is effectively phasing out the tier and further reducing songwriter royalties. The change follows Spotify’s decision in late 2023 to integrate audiobooks into its Premium Individual, Family and Duo plans. These plans were subsequently reclassified as ‘bundled subscription offerings’

item.title: Soundstripe, PopArabia launch MENA songwriting camps in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Soundstripe has partnered with Abu Dhabi-based independent music company PopArabia to run a series of songwriting camps aimed at artists and songwriters from the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), marking the US music licensing platform’s first such initiative outside the United States. The first camp was held in Abu Dhabi in October and brought together artists from the United Arab Emirates, Egypt, Algeria, Morocco, Iraq, Lebanon and Sudan.
